formula: nonlinear Joyner-Boore attenuation of log10(accel) in Richter and distance, random effects on all four coefficients by Quake with a diagonal covariance
notes: NONLINEAR: log10(accel) = phi1 + phi2*Richter - log10(sqrt(distance^2 + exp(phi3))) - phi4*sqrt(distance^2 + exp(phi3)) (Joyner and Boore 1981; Davidian and Giltinan 1995, sec. 11.4). Pinheiro and Bates (2000, ch. 6 exercise 3(c)) fit it by nlme with random effects for all coefficients and a diagonal Psi, then drop random effects by anova (3(d)) and add soil to a coefficient (3(f)). Outside check: the model replaces the reading's log-linear substitute; Stata's menl manual (examples 6-8) fits reduced versions with the same response and grouping, which file no row.

formula: nonlinear Paris-law crack growth of relLength in cycles, Path-specific C and m - 1 jointly normal
notes: NONLINEAR: integrated Paris-law crack growth with two random parameters per test unit (Path). Lu and Meeker (1993, Technometrics 35, sec. 5.1) fit this degradation path model to the 21 fatigue-crack paths; the help page states no model. Outside check: the model replaces the linear placeholder.

formula: nonlinear glucose pulse phi1 + phi2*Time^3*exp(-phi3*Time), random phi1 and phi2 by Subject and by Subject:Date
notes: NONLINEAR: glucose = phi1 + phi2*Time^3*exp(-phi3*Time) (Hand and Crowder 1996, Example 8.4). Pinheiro and Bates (2000, ch. 8 exercise 3(c)) fit a two-level nlme with random phi1 and phi2 at Subject and Date within Subject, phi3 fixed and unstructured covariances; later items try diagonal covariances, CAR1 errors and a Date effect on the fixed effects. Outside check: the model replaces the linear placeholder; exercise 3(g)'s Hand and Crowder model and Stata's menl examples 21-22 share the response and file no row.

NIST Alaska-pipeline ultrasonic defect depths, field vs lab measurements taken in six batches (107 rows). Faraway fits a calibration regression Lab ~ Field ignoring batch; rendered with a random intercept on the measurement Batch. The NIST handbook (4.6.2.2) treats Batch as a nuisance factor: it fits a line per batch, finds the batches homogeneous and pools them. Retained Batch assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of measurement batches; this remains unverified. Outside check: stands; GPT filed it flat, kept as a cluster that repeats while the source treats rows as independent.

formula: sbvalue ~ treatment + baseline*(week + I(week^2)) + (0 + week + I(week^2)|subject)
notes: Help page describes a longitudinal RCT of methylprednisolone for severe alcoholic hepatitis (serum bilirubin weekly, weeks 0-4; Vonesh and Chinchilli 1997) but gives no formula. Shi and Ojeda (2004, J. Multivariate Anal. 91, sec. 6, eq. 30), as GPT cites them, fit treatment additively, baseline by linear and quadratic week, and correlated linear and quadratic subject slopes without a random intercept, whose variance was zero in eqs. 28-29; the paper was not read here (the publisher blocks scripts). The fields hold the nearest form, week|subject with an intercept; the quadratic terms are in the formula. baseline is the pre-treatment value, a covariate. Outside check: the paper's model replaces the reading's treatment by week growth.

Help page gives no model; alpha-design multi-environment trial (Buntaran et al. 2020, Crop Science 60). Their equation 1, as GPT cites it, fits the three zones fixed and location, replicate within location, incomplete block, genotype, genotype by zone and genotype by location random, the compound-symmetry case; the paper was not read here (the publisher blocks scripts). Their stagewise analysis fits each location apart first (equation 2), a subset fit. Outside check: genotype by zone and by location added, as the second reading and adjudication #22 suggested.

Multi-environment tomato trial (Ortiz et al. 2007); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling ortiz.tomato.covs), no mixed model, and the paper fits factorial regression and PLS. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design; one yield per gen x env, some cells missing. weight is an alternate response, ignored. Outside check: no published model, the crossed intercepts inferred from the design.

Help page fits Seshu and Cady's model 1, lm(yield ~ rad + mint + I(mint^2)), and lm(yield ~ mint + I(mint^2)), both without random effects, and calls the quadratic senseless; rendered without the quadratic term, with locations nested in countries random (adjudication #22). loc labels are unique across countries. Outside check: no published model, the nesting inferred.

Lattice-square variety trial of 49 soybeans in 4 reps (Weiss & Cox 1939). Help fits a fixed lm/asreml yield ~ rep + rep:col + rep:row + gen (matching Weiss table 7). Mixed rendering treats the incomplete row/column blocks within rep as random, rep and genotype fixed; rep:col and rep:row are composites built from their parts. rep is a design factor by the five-level rule: four reps (R1 to R4), fitted as fixed in the help's lm and asreml calls. Outside check: no published model, since both calls fit every block term fixed; GPT made rep random by the fixed-block rule, and it stays fixed by the five-level rule.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ x + block + (1 | var)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: diseased shoots r of the n shoots per plot. boot help: randomized block design, 45 sugar-cane varieties x 4 blocks; no model fitted. Rendered as a binomial GLMM with variety random (the aim is to classify the 45 varieties by resistance), block fixed and x (stem pieces planted) a covariate. block is a design factor by the five-level rule: four blocks (A to D), described in words only and fitted as random by no cited source. Retained var assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger cultivar population; this remains unverified. Outside check: stands.
